test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 18 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is the Directive Principle of State Policy mentioned under Article 48A of the Indian Constitution?

options.text: Protection and improvement of the environment

solution:
The correct answer is __**Protection and improvement of the environment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 48A** of the **Indian Constitution** is a part of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), which enjoins the state to protect and improve the environment and safeguard the forests and wildlife of the country.
 
• This article was inserted into the Constitution by the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**, which emphasized environmental protection as a fundamental directive for the state.
 
• The provision underlines the responsibility of the state to ensure a healthy environment, including the improvement of ecosystems and natural habitats. *Hence, statement 4 is correct.*
 
• Article 48A aligns with the broad objectives of sustainable development and recognizes the critical importance of environmental conservation for future generations.
 
• The inclusion of this article underscores India's commitment to global environmental concerns and its intent to integrate sustainable development into policymaking.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP):**

 
 
• The DPSPs are non-justiciable provisions listed in **Part IV of the Indian Constitution**. These principles are fundamental in the governance of the country and aim to achieve socio-economic justice.
 
• While not enforceable in a court of law, they act as guidelines for the state to implement policies and laws that promote the welfare of the people.
 
 
 
• **42nd Amendment Act, 1976:**
 
 
• The 42nd Amendment Act is also known as the "**Mini Constitution**" due to the wide range of changes it brought to the Indian Constitution.
 
• It added **Article 48A** under the DPSP and **Article 51A(g)** under Fundamental Duties, making environmental protection a responsibility of both the state and citizens.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of Article 48A:**
 
 
• **Focus:** Aimed at the protection and improvement of the **environment**, including forests and wildlife.
 
• **Importance:** It establishes the foundation for the enactment of environmental laws and regulations in India, like the **Environment Protection Act, 1986**.
 
• **Global Relevance:** Aligns with global environmental principles and India's commitment to international conventions on environmental protection.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Relevant DPSPs:**

 
 
• **Article 40:** Relates to the organization of **Gram Panchayats**, encouraging decentralized governance. *This is not related to Article 48A and is incorrect.*
 
• **Article 47:** Directs the state to raise the level of **nutrition** and improve public health. *This is not associated with environmental protection and is incorrect.*
 
• **Article 39A:** Provides for **legal aid** to weaker sections to promote justice on equal footing. *This is unrelated to environmental protection and is incorrect.*
 
 
 
• **Environmental Laws in India:**
 
 
• **Environment Protection Act, 1986:** Enacted to implement decisions of the United Nations Conference on the Human Environment held in 1972.
 
• **Wildlife Protection Act, 1972:** Aimed at protecting wildlife and their habitats.
 
• **Forest Conservation Act, 1980:** Focused on restricting deforestation and promoting forest conservation.
